text: The effective concentration of a component in a solution, a = X γ; equal to the mole fraction for ideal mixing.
Factor describing deviation from ideal mixing; γ > 1 for positive deviations.
Aluminium in tetrahedral (IV) and octahedral (VI) coordination.
Sum of oxide weight percentages of an analysis; ~100% for anhydrous phases.
Composition recalculated without H₂O (sum of other oxides normalised).
Atoms per formula unit: number of cations in the mineral formula normalised to a fixed number of oxygens or cations.
Equilibrium whose composition depends mainly on pressure; used to estimate P at known T.
Method generating normally distributed random numbers from pairs of uniform random numbers.
Root-finding method that repeatedly halves an interval in which a function changes sign; always converges.
The experiments (or natural samples) used to fit an empirical equation.
The compositional (and P–T) space covered by a calibration dataset; LithoPT measures it with the Mahalanobis distance.
Number of atoms of a cation divided by the total number of cations (anhydrous).
Condition that positive and negative charges in a mineral formula are equal; used to estimate Fe³⁺.
cov(T, P)/(σ_T σ_P); ±1 perfect correlation, 0 none.
Measure of joint variability of two quantities.
Cr/(Cr + Al), molar.
Concentration ratio of an element between two phases, e.g. D_Mg<sup>ol/liq</sup>.
Squared Mahalanobis distance (Chapter 9).
Estimation of Fe³⁺ from stoichiometry and charge balance (Section 4.2).
Set of solutions from all compatible thermometer–barometer pairs; its spread measures model-choice uncertainty.
Product of activities of products over reactants, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient.
Reaction exchanging two cations between phases, with small volume change; a good thermometer.
Total iron expressed as FeO.
Fayalite–magnetite–quartz oxygen buffer; ΔFMQ is log fO₂ relative to it.
Oxygen fugacity, the effective partial pressure of oxygen; describes the redox state.
Garnet–Al₂SiO₅–plagioclase–quartz barometer.
Equation estimating melt water content.
Distribution (exchange) coefficient, e.g. (Fe/Mg)^A/(Fe/Mg)^B.
Comparison of measured and expected K_D to test whether two phases were in equilibrium.
Kilobar; 1 kbar = 0.1 GPa ≈ 3.3–3.7 km of crust.
Distance of a point from the mean of a multivariate distribution in units of standard deviation, accounting for correlations.
Mg/(Mg + Fe) molar (often ×100).
Repeated calculation with randomly perturbed inputs to estimate output uncertainty.
Reaction changing modal amounts of phases, usually with large ΔV; a good barometer.
Equation estimating oxygen fugacity.
Broad physical bounds outside which results are flagged.
Root-mean-square error between calculated and reference values.
Thermometer based on the solubility of a phase in a melt that is saturated in it.
Standard error of estimate of a regression: scatter of calibration data about the fitted equation.
Starting value of a pseudo-random number generator; the same seed gives the same Monte Carlo sample.
Miscibility gap between two coexisting phases of the same structure.
Reference state for thermodynamic properties; here the pure phase at P and T.
Mineral formula expressed as cations per formula unit.
Equilibrium whose composition depends mainly on temperature; used to estimate T at known P.
Thermometer based on the temperature-dependent concentration of a trace element in a buffered mineral.
Mole fraction of component i.
